- Answer: OpenAI dominates news attention, with 255,044 of 336,283 combined articles (75.8%) from 2024-06 to 2026-05 [c1]. Anthropic has 70,192 (20.9%) [c1] and Google DeepMind 11,047 (3.3%) [c1]. All three are rising, and Anthropic is rising fastest [c1].
- Decision: Treat OpenAI as the default benchmark for media share. Treat Anthropic as the fast-closing challenger, and do not read DeepMind's small count as the whole of Google's AI coverage.
- Confidence: medium - the counts are measured and coverage passed its checks [c1]. The tone labels and the term match are unverified, and the data ends 2026-05.
- What would change it: A check of "deepmind" and "anthropic" matches showing off-topic hits, or Google-branded AI coverage that does not use "DeepMind".

## What the data shows
Window: 2024-06-01 to 2026-05-31, monthly, 24 months [c1]. The newest month, June 2026, is censored by the tool [c1].

| Term | Articles | Share | Critical | Critical share of articles |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| openai | 255,044 [c1] | 75.8% [c1] | 190,992 [c1] | 74.9% (est., computed from [c1]) |
| anthropic | 70,192 [c1] | 20.9% [c1] | 51,731 [c1] | 73.7% (est., computed from [c1]) |
| deepmind | 11,047 [c1] | 3.3% [c1] | 8,688 [c1] | 78.6% (est., computed from [c1]) |

- `most_covered` is openai [c1]. `combined_articles` is 336,283 [c1]. The combined figure is a sum of per-term counts. An article that mentions more than one term is counted once per term, so it is not a de-duplicated total (the tool does not say; this is my reading).
- Growth and direction as reported by the tool: openai 2.06, rising [c1]; anthropic 5.68, rising [c1]; deepmind 1.4, rising [c1]. The tool does not define the growth statistic in this output. My reading is a late-period to early-period ratio, which I have not verified.
- Tone ratio as reported: openai 0.39 [c1], anthropic 0.45 [c1], deepmind 0.18 [c1]. The definition is not given in the output. The monthly points carry separate positive and negative counts, and those counts do not sum to the article count. Tone is therefore a model-assigned label, and I cannot state its exact definition.
- Against the baseline, `vs_baseline` is 0.67 for openai [c1], 0.78 for anthropic [c1] and 0.31 for deepmind [c1]. The baseline is not defined in the output, so I do not interpret these values.
- Peak months:
  - OpenAI: 2026-04, 20,792 articles [c1].
  - Anthropic: 2026-04, 11,550 articles [c1].
  - DeepMind: 2026-02, 710 articles [c1].
- Anthropic's step change came in 2026-02: 9,497 articles, against 2,724 in 2026-01 [c1]. That is about 3.5x (est., computed from [c1]). The data cannot say what caused it.

## Method and limits
- Window: 2024-06-01 to 2026-05-31, monthly [c1]. The tool censored June 2026 and later because ingest lags publication [c1]. Today is 2026-10-23, so the gap is about 145 days (est., computed from dates). Nothing from June to October 2026 is covered.
- Lanes: one lane, news (corpus table `the index`) [c1]. Research and other lanes were not queried.
- Coverage: the tool reports all tables passed strict index partition reads and historical row floors, at 107.1% of the expected rows [c1]. It also says this is a reachability check and not proof that ingest is complete.
- Match mode: the terms were openai, anthropic and deepmind. The tool does not state whether matching is on the name in text, the title or an entity tag. I cannot confirm this.
- Common-word caveat: the tool warns that a term that is also a common word will over-count [c1]. "Anthropic" is also an adjective meaning human-centred, and "deepmind" is partly a compound of two words. I did not check this against the sources panel, so I cannot say how much of the counts is off-topic.
- Overlap: articles mentioning more than one company are counted for each. Shares are shares of the summed term counts, not of unique articles.
- The counts are attention: how many articles mention a name. They are not importance, quality, reach or reader numbers, and they do not show sentiment toward a company.
- Interpretation, not data: my readings of the growth statistic, the "critical" label and the DeepMind–Google relationship. DeepMind is only one Google AI brand, so its low share does not measure Google's AI coverage.
- Cannot be answered here: causes of the 2026-02 jump, publisher and country mix, the definition of tone and baseline, and anything after 2026-05.

## Method and limits

The source window runs from 2024-06-01 to 2026-06-01, with the end exclusive; that is 144 days before today, 2026-10-23 (dates and interval from [c1]). The comparison is monthly. Although monthly rows are marked not partial, the call-level note says the newest month holds only a fraction of a normal month due to ingest lag. May 2026 is therefore shown in the export but omitted from the chart and endpoint trend reading [c1].

Lane: news. The reported news table passed strict index partition reads and historical row-floor checks, with 107.1% of expected rows; the source explicitly says this is not proof of ingest completeness [c1]. Counts measure matching articles in the corpus, not importance, audience reach, unique readers, or public opinion. “Rising,” growth, tone ratio, priority, and critical classification are source outputs; their formulas or definitions are not supplied. The recommendation to allocate monitoring by volume is interpretation of those outputs. Common-word matches may inflate counts, particularly where the term has other meanings [c1].
